summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted for evaluation of bright red blood per rectum, which occurred in the setting of known ulcerative colitis and cirrhosis. He had four episodes of hematochezia the day before admission but no further bleeding during the hospital stay. Workup revealed stable hemoglobin, no signs of variceal bleeding, and no indication for urgent endoscopy. The bleeding was attributed to colitis, and mesalamine was continued. His cirrhosis remained stable with mild ascites and no hepatic encephalopathy; lactulose was held initially and restarted prior to discharge. He remained on prophylactic rifaximin and ciprofloxacin. Pain management continued with tramadol. He was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up planned in transplant, hepatology, and gastroenterology clinics within one week.
